description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and Accuracy for three different accuracy metrics. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.95 to 0.99, with visible tick marks at intervals of 0.01 at 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, and 0.99, while the 0.98 tick label is obscured by a grey rectangle. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The "Final Acc" data is represented by a solid blue line with circle markers and error bars; it begins at an accuracy of approximately 0.90 at an initial confidence of 0.95, dips to roughly 0.86 at 0.96, rises to a peak of about 0.93 at the 0.98 mark, and ends at approximately 0.87 at 0.99. The "Δ Acc" data is shown as a dashed orange line with diamond markers and error bars, starting at approximately 0.90 at 0.95, decreasing to about 0.86 at 0.96, rising slightly to 0.88 at 0.97, remaining steady at roughly 0.87 at 0.98, and declining to approximately 0.75 at 0.99. The "Initial Acc" data is depicted by a dash-dot green line with square markers and error bars; it starts at 0.0 at 0.95, remains flat at 0.0 at 0.96, and then steadily increases, reaching approximately 0.01 at 0.97, 0.05 at 0.98, and ending at its peak of roughly 0.12 at 0.99.
